title.narrative: Emergency Response to floods in Florencia, Caquetá

description.narrative:
This emergency grant is in response to serious flooding which occurred in the town of Florencia in the Department of Caquetá on 21st May 2010 which has affected families in a number of communities and municipalities in both urban and rural areas. In the town of Florencia alone 2,552 families (approx. 12,780 people) have been affected and 800 houses partially destroyed. One child died and two people are missing. These are the worst floods to hit the region in the last few years and the Colombian Institute of Hydrology, Meteorology and Environment (IDEAM) has warned the population of more heavy rains to come with a risk of storms.
Our partner, Pastoral Social in Florencia, responded immediately to the disaster distributing clothes and medicines donated by the community to 32 affected families in the town of Florencia. The diocese now requires further support to reach more affected families who have been forced to evacuate from their homes. This grant is a contribution to the diocese of Florencia’s relief efforts to support 200 families (approx 1,000 people) with essential food and non food items. A number of the beneficiaries of the CAFOD / EU funded livelihoods programme (COL160 / COL168) have been affected by the floods and they will be included in this project. This includes members of six of the businesses in Florencia including the Metal Recycling business (one member’s home was destroyed), the greengrocer, chicken selling business, clothes making and restaurant.
